page: Amazon Web Services m6g.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features AWS Graviton2 processors built on the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture. The instance is allocated 4 dedicated vCPUs operating at 2.5 GHz with 1 thread per core (4 physical cores total). Each core is equipped with 64 KB of L1 data cache and 1 MB of L2 cache, backed by a 32 MB shared L3 cache. Memory capacity is 16.0 GB, providing a standard general-purpose ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware configuration does not bundle local disk storage or dedicated GPU accelerators, and baseline networking capability is 1 Gbps.

Benchmark outcomes show moderate efficiency in raw single-core tasks alongside lower relative throughput in intensive compute suites. In stress-ng evaluations, the single-core score reaches 1489.98 (middle 50%), while multi-core performance falls into the lower 25% at 5934.04. Synthetic suites like Geekbench yield a single-core score of 954.0 and a multi-core score of 3166.0, reflecting the architectural characteristics of 4 physical Neoverse-N1 cores without simultaneous multithreading. Uncached large-block memory bandwidth demonstrates solid metrics at 71.14 GB/sec for reads and 34.79 GB/sec for writes, both falling within the middle 50% percentile.

In operational and workload benchmarks, m6g.xlarge achieves 4.48 million Redis SET operations per second and a static web serving throughput of 4.91 GB/sec. Data compression performance includes 19.78 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip and 29.13 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Due to the lack of x86 vector extensions (AVX/AVX-512) and dedicated accelerators, small LLM inference rates remain limited, recording 143.49 tokens per second for prompt processing and 55.22 tokens per second for text generation on a 135M parameter model.

Without integrated local NVMe storage, persistent storage relies entirely on external network-attached volumes. This instance offers architectural power efficiency for ARM-native workflows. The m6g.xlarge is well positioned for containerized microservices, application servers, intermediate caching tiers, low-to-medium volume web serving, and general cloud workloads that benefit from consistent physical core allocation without requiring high instruction set specialization.

Configured with 16.0 GB of RAM (4.0 GB per core) and running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it contains no integrated local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and a 1 Gbps baseline network link. Benchmark testing reveals middle-tier single-core CPU throughput (1489.98 on stress-ng) alongside stable uncached memory bandwidth of 71.14 GB/sec read and 34.79 GB/sec write.
